Disability ID (disabilityid.co.uk) - Sitewide "Apply" CTA Copy Test

Convert.com exp. 100052760 · QA date: 2026-09-02 · Tester: automated (Playwright) + manual live-DOM verification

125 / 147 passed across 7 browser/device projects (21 intentionally skipped - the inner-page FAQ check only runs for control/v1 by design, since it verifies the same mechanism already covered for v2-v4 elsewhere). What this test does

Replaces the visible text of every primary "Apply" CTA sitewide (control: "Apply") with softer/ gain-framed copy, text-only - keeping href, styling, size, colour, case, icon and hover state identical. New users only, sitewide, excluding the application funnel (forms.disabilityid.co.uk). 4 variations:

Real "Apply" CTA locations (live-verified)

  1. Header/nav button (.right-nav, always visible)
  2. Hero section button, next to hero "Renew"
  3. Mobile-only button inside the bottom SECTION.apply CTA block (.hide-desktop; its desktop sibling already reads "Start my application" and is correctly never touched)

No footer "Apply" CTA exists on the live site today - the ticket's dev notes mention one ("the footer button"), but the real <footer> only has a "Renew" link, a newsletter signup form, and an unrelated "National Carers Card" button (different brand). Recommend confirming with the ticket author whether this is outdated copy or whether a footer CTA is expected to be added before launch.

Several other buttons share the exact same /apply href but different visible text and correctly stay untouched: "Renew" (hero, nav, footer), "Join 300,000+ card holders", "Start my application", and inline FAQ-page content mentions of the word "apply".

Finding: intermittent failure - Safari Desktop, v3, mobile-only CTA

On Safari Desktop (WebKit) only, variation v3, the mobile-only "Apply" button inside SECTION.apply occasionally rendered as unreplaced "Apply" instead of "Get my card" on initial page load. Re-running this exact test in isolation: 1st re-run failed, 2nd re-run passed - confirming this is a genuine intermittent timing issue, not a one-off fluke or a broken selector (the same check passes reliably on Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Mobile Chrome, Mobile Safari and Tablet).

Root cause (see code review below): the variation JS uses a single-shot waitForElement poll that fires updateApplyButton() exactly once, as soon as the first a[href*="apply"] exists (typically the header button, which renders almost immediately). There is no MutationObserver or retry to catch this specific below-the-fold button if it is not yet fully settled in the DOM at that instant - WebKit's script/render timing appears to occasionally lose this race. This does not affect the 2 primary CTAs (header, hero), which passed 100% of the time across all 7 projects.

Application funnel exclusion

Confirmed: forms.disabilityid.co.uk/apply is unaffected - Convert's snippet is not even installed on that subdomain (different body markup entirely, no cre-t-02 class regardless of the forced variation param).

Code review (against team checklist)

#Checklist itemVerdictNotes
1Variation class name presentPASSaddClass('body','cre-t-02') on every variation's init. Constant is identical across all 4 files (harmless - Convert loads one variation's script per visitor) but means body class alone can't distinguish which variation is live for prod debugging.
2Check element doesn't already exist before insertingGAPinsertAfter always calls insertAdjacentHTML('afterend', ...) with no guard against re-insertion. Harmless today (runs once per load) but unprotected if ever re-invoked.
3Intervals cleared via setTimeoutPASSwaitForElement's interval is cleared on match and via the 15s timeout fallback.
4Event listeners/observers behind a re-entry guardN/ANo listeners or observers in this code.
5Fallback when hide-condition code doesn't fireGAPConfirmed live: no MutationObserver/retry means the mobile-only CTA can intermittently miss the swap (see Safari Desktop/v3 finding above). If waitForElement times out after 15s, the page silently stays on control-like "Apply" text with no monitoring signal.
6Observer/scroll-detector debounceN/ANo observer/scroll listener present.
7Observers disconnected after a conditionGAPNo MutationObserver used at all - recommend adding one (auto-disconnected after ~5s or first successful pass) to close the intermittent-miss gap found above.
8Remove unnecessary functionsPASSAll helper functions are used; no dead code.
9Cache URL fetches in session storageN/ANo network fetch/XHR in this code.
10Loops clearedPASSSame interval-clearing logic as #3.
11Never use dynamic selectorsPASS*a[href*="apply"] is a stable, meaningful selector (not a Webflow auto-generated id). It incidentally matches other buttons sharing the same href, but the dual text-match check correctly excludes them - verified live. *Relies on exact-text coincidence protection rather than a dedicated class, which is workable but slightly fragile long-term.

Recommendation: the intermittent Safari Desktop/v3 failure and the #5/#7 gaps are the same underlying issue - add a short-lived MutationObserver (disconnect after first successful pass or ~5s) instead of relying solely on the one-shot waitForElement poll, to close this race before it reaches production.
